Yitzhak Rabin: Prime Minister of Israel (1974–1977; 1992–1995)

What is the atomic number of Magnesium?
Magnesium is a chemical element; it has symbol Mg and atomic number 12.
In what year was Josef Mengele born?
Josef Mengele: Before the war, Mengele received doctorates in anthropology and medicine, and he began a career as a researcher.
In what year was Fructose discovered?
Fructose, or fruit sugar, is a common monosaccharide, i.e. a simple sugar.
In what year was Gallium discovered?
Gallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ga and atomic number 31.

Who is credited with discovering Scandium?
Scandium: Lars Fredrik Nilson. Scandium is a chemical element; it has symbol Sc and atomic number 21.
Despite the conspiracy buzz, this violet compound is mass-produced, sold to the public, and not a controlled substance — its hemostatic derivative is carbazochrome. What is it?
Adrenochrome is a chemical compound produced by the oxidation of adrenaline (epinephrine).
This parasitic intestinal illness, caused by Entamoeba histolytica, can produce cysts that survive for weeks in soil or nearly an hour under fingernails — what is it called?
Amoebiasis is an infection of the intestines caused by a parasitic amoeba Entamoeba histolytica.
Its Latin name means 'water-carrier,' and this zodiac constellation sits between Capricornus and Pisces, in a region of the sky nicknamed 'the Sea' for its watery neighbors — which constellation?

Aquarius (constellation) is an equatorial constellation of the zodiac, between Capricornus and Pisces. Its name is Latin for "water-carrier" or "cup-carrier", and its traditional astrological symbol is (♒︎), a representation of water.

With the symbol Ba and atomic number 56, this soft, silvery alkaline earth metal is so reactive it's never found free in nature, and takes its name from a Greek word meaning 'heavy' — name this element?
Barium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ba and atomic number 56.
Known scientifically as Simuliidae, this family of small biting insects includes more than 2,200 named species, all but a handful belonging to a single genus — what are they commonly called?
Black fly (sometimes called buffalo gnats, turkey gnats, or white socks) are flies in the family Simuliidae of the Culicomorpha infraorder.
Meaning 'thunder lizard' in Greek, this sauropod dinosaur genus was described by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1879 from a partial, skull-less skeleton found in Wyoming's Como Bluff — what dinosaur is it?

Brontosaurus (literally 'thunder lizard', from the Greek words bront, 'thunder', and saros, 'lizard') is a genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur that lived in present-day United States during the Late Jurassic period.
Its name comes from the Latin for "coal," and one of its isotopes decays with a 5,700-year half-life that lets scientists date ancient remains — which element is it?
Carbon (from Latin carbo 'coal') is a chemical element; it has symbol C and atomic number 6.

Doctors monitor blood levels every two days when giving this last-resort antibiotic, since its side effects include bone marrow suppression and, in infants, a swollen-stomach condition known as gray baby syndrome — what drug is it?
Chloramphenicol is an antibiotic useful for the treatment of a number of bacterial infections.

With just two living species — the Sunda and Philippine varieties — these Southeast Asian gliders are arboreal primatomorphs more closely related to primates than to any other animal — what is this group called?
Colugo are arboreal gliding primatomorphs that are native to Southeast Asia.

This practice and field of study focuses on techniques for secure communication in the presence of adversaries, sitting at the intersection of mathematics, computer science, and electrical engineering — what's the field called?
Cryptography is the practice and study of techniques for secure communication in the presence of adversarial behavior.
Caused by a Corynebacterium bacterium, this infection can spin a tough grey 'pseudomembrane' across the throat that slowly chokes off the airway — what is it?
Diphtheria is an infection caused by the bacterium Corynebacterium diphtheriae. The pseudomembrane can grow to cover a wide area of the throat, leading to strangulation and death.
These extinct flightless giants of Madagascar — possibly the largest birds ever, laying the biggest eggs of any amniote — vanished around 1000 AD, likely thanks to humans. What are they called?
Elephant bird are extinct flightless birds belonging to the order Aepyornithiformes that were native to the island of Madagascar.

Built by a consortium of Airbus, BAE Systems and Leonardo for four NATO nations, this twin-engine canard delta-wing fighter grew out of the 1983 Future European Fighter Aircraft programme — which jet?
Eurofighter Typhoon is a European multinational twin-engine, supersonic, canard delta wing, multirole fighter.

This genetic neurodevelopmental disorder causes a long, narrow face, large ears, and unusually flexible fingers, with males typically far more affected than females and average IQ under 55 in affected boys — what's the condition?

Fragile X syndrome (FXS) is a genetic neurodevelopmental disorder. The average IQ in males with FXS is under 55, while affected females tend to be in the borderline to normal range, typically around 70–85.

He shared a 1951 Nobel for synthesizing ten transuranium elements and developed the actinide concept that reshaped the periodic table; this American chemist later advised ten US presidents on nuclear policy — who was he?

Glenn T. Seaborg (April 19, 1912 - February 25, 1999) was an American chemist whose involvement in the synthesis, discovery and investigation of ten transuranium elements earned him a share of the 1951 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
The first Professor of the Public Understanding of Mathematics at Cambridge, she's also a BBC broadcaster who explores the math behind human relationships — who is she?
Hannah Fry (born 21 February 1984) is a British mathematician, author and broadcaster.
This common household insect, likely originating in the Middle East, mates only once in her lifetime but stores the sperm to fertilize repeated batches of about 100 eggs — what insect is it?
Housefly (Musca domestica) is a fly of the suborder Cyclorrhapha.
Patented in 1961 and approved two years later, this nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug works by blocking the enzyme cyclooxygenase to cut prostaglandin production — what drug is it?
Indometacin is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) commonly used as a prescription medication to reduce fever, pain, stiffness, and swelling from inflammation.
This British chemical engineer founded and leads a global chemicals conglomerate in 1998, and was briefly the richest person in the UK before shifting his tax residence to Monaco. Who is he?
Jim Ratcliffe (born 18 October 1952) is a British billionaire, chemical engineer, and businessman.
About the size of a domestic chicken, these flightless New Zealand natives turn out to be more closely related to Madagascar's extinct elephant birds than to the giant moa — what are they?
Kiwi (bird) are flightless birds endemic to New Zealand of the order Apterygiformes.
Found in all land animals with internal skeletons, this fibrous band connects bones to other bones and, in birds and dinosaurs, secures flight feathers in place — what is it?
Ligament is a type of fibrous connective tissue in the body that connects bones to other bones.
Found in nearly every animal cell but rare in plants, this membrane-bound organelle acts as the cell's degradation center, breaking proteins, sugars, and fats into their building blocks — what is it?
Lysosome (/lassom/) is a membrane-bound organelle that is found in all animal cells (except red blood cells), and rarely in plant cells.

Designed as both fighter and ground-attack aircraft (hence the F/A designation), this all-weather supersonic, carrier-capable twin-engined jet was derived from the YF-17 and developed for the Navy. What aircraft is this?

McDonnell Douglas F/A-18 Hornet is an all-weather supersonic, twin-engined, carrier-capable, multirole combat aircraft, designed as both a fighter and ground attack aircraft (hence the F/A designation).

Attaching to its host tree through a structure called the haustorium to steal water and nutrients, this hemiparasitic plant has one species native to the British Isles and much of Europe — what is it?
Mistletoe is the common name for obligate hemiparasitic plants in the order Santalales.
A white crystalline solid built from two fused benzene rings, this aromatic compound is the main ingredient of traditional mothballs and has an odor you can smell at just 0.08 ppm. What is it?
Naphthalene is an organic compound with the chemical formula C10H8.
Belonging to the beech family and encompassing about 500 species across the Northern Hemisphere, this hardwood tree or shrub bears a distinctive nut held in a small cup — name the tree?
Oak is a hardwood tree or shrub in the genus Quercus of the beech family.
Its name comes from the Greek for "from everywhere" because it turns up in nearly all foods — and this B vitamin lets animals build coenzyme A for energy. Which vitamin is it?
Pantothenic acid (vitamin B5) is a B vitamin and an essential nutrient.

Fill in the blank: “____ (PD) is a benign, acquired penile connective tissue disease characterized by the occurrence of fibrotic plaques within the tunica albuginea - the dense elastic covering of the corpora cavernosa.”

Peyronie's disease (PD) is a benign, acquired penile connective tissue disease characterized by the occurrence of fibrotic plaques within the tunica albuginea - the dense elastic covering of the corpora cavernosa. The plaques cause abnormal curvature, pain, penile deformities (e.g., narrowing or indentation), and usually erectile dysfunction, particularly during erection.
Carrying minor-planet number 134340, this icy Kuiper-belt world has about one-sixth the Moon's mass and got demoted when astronomers rewrote the rules — what is it?
Pluto (minor-planet number 134340) is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, a ring of bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
Belonging to the rose family, this flowering tree species gives us most plums, including the greengage and damson varieties — which species is it?
Prunus domestica is a species of flowering plant in the family Rosaceae.
With roughly 12,000 living species split across four classic orders — including the single-species tuatara branch — what ectothermic class is this?
Reptile are tetrapod vertebrate animals with an ectothermic metabolism and amniotic development.

Known from complete specimens found in Bolivia, this extinct armored jawless fish from the Ordovician period resembled a slender tadpole with eyes set like car headlamps on its oversized head — what is it?
Sacabambaspis is an extinct genus of armored jawless fish which lived in the Ordovician period.

Essentially plasma with the clotting factors and cells removed, this pale yellow fluid still carries antibodies, hormones, and electrolytes and is central to typing tests done before a transfusion — what is it?
Serum (blood) is the fluid and solvent component of blood which does not play a role in clotting.
This use of the human voice for language ranges from informing and persuading to simply asking or declaring, combining vowels and consonants into meaningful words — what is it called?
Speech is the use of the human voice as a medium for language.
Among the most experienced spacewalkers in history, this NASA astronaut logged over 62 hours across nine spacewalks — the most of any woman — who is she?
Sunita Williams (ne Pandya; born September 19, 1965) is a retired United States Navy captain and former NASA astronaut.
Raised in Michigan with little schooling, he sold his first inventions by age 22 and moved to New York to chase engineering — going on to become one of America's most famous inventors. Who?
Thomas Edison (February 11, 1847 - October 18, 1931) was an American inventor and businessman.
First isolated as a metal in 1783, this element is drawn from ores like scheelite and wolframite — the latter lending it an alternative name. Which metal is it?
Tungsten (also called wolfram) is a chemical element; it has symbol W (from) and atomic number 74.
Named from a French verb meaning 'to see,' this term describes the practice of secretly watching others in intimate moments, often labeled 'Peeping Tom' behavior — what is it?
Voyeurism is the habit of clandestine watching other people engaged in intimate behaviors, such as undressing, sexual activity, or other actions of a private nature, commonly for sexual stimulation.

Nicknamed the 'Sleeping Dragon' during his years in seclusion, this Chinese strategist was sought out three times by a warlord before becoming chancellor of the Shu Han state and, later, regent to its young second emperor — who is he?

Zhuge Liang (181 AD - September or October 234 AD), courtesy name Kongming, was a Chinese statesman and strategist who lived through the collapse of the Eastern Han dynasty and became the principal architect of the Shu Han state.

Typically affecting women between 35 and 50, this uterine condition occurs when endometrial-like tissue grows within the muscular wall of the uterus, causing painful, heavy periods — what is it called?
Adenomyosis: Extension of endometrial tissue into the myometrium.
On 18 March 1965, this Soviet cosmonaut became the first person to walk in space, spending over twelve minutes outside his capsule during a Voskhod mission — who is he?
Caused by the parasite Entamoeba histolytica, this intestinal infection can spread to the liver and trigger abscesses there even without any prior diarrhea — what condition is it?
Amoebiasis: Human disease caused by amoeba protists.
This self-taught Dutch draper turned lensmaker began exploring microbial life with his own single-lensed microscopes in the 1670s, earning him the title 'Father of Microbiology' — who was he?
Writing in 499 CE that he was 23 years old, this pioneering Indian scholar's explicit discussion of the relativity of motion marks him as an early physicist too — who was he?
Sold under the brand name Lioresal, this muscle relaxant treats spasticity from spinal cord injuries or MS and is sometimes used off-label for alcohol withdrawal — what is it?
Baclofen: Gabapentinoid and Skeletal Muscle Relaxant.
This steroid medication treats everything from rheumatoid arthritis to psoriasis, and can even be given to speed a premature baby's lung development before birth — what is it?
Betamethasone: Steroid medication. It can be taken by mouth, injected into a muscle, or applied to the skin, typically in cream, lotion, or liquid forms.
A twinjet successor to a trijet predecessor, this American narrow-body airliner entered commercial service with Eastern Air Lines on New Year's Day 1983. Which aircraft?
Too small to fuse hydrogen but massive enough to briefly burn deuterium, these objects between 13 and 80 Jupiter masses cool over time through spectral classes M, L, T, and Y — what are they called?
With more than 220 species and over 26,000 registered cultivars, this flowering plant genus includes the very species whose leaves are processed into tea worldwide — which genus?
Camellia: Genus of flowering plants in the tea family.
Publishing a landmark 1912 paper on 'vital amines,' this Polish biochemist helped pioneer the concept now known as vitamins while researching pellagra and rickets — who is he?
Released by OpenAI in November 2022 and built on generative pre-trained transformers, this chatbot is widely credited with setting off the current AI boom. Name it.

ChatGPT is a generative AI chatbot developed by OpenAI, originally released in November 2022, using large language models — specifically generative pre-trained transformers — and it accelerated the ongoing AI boom.

An American naturalist who surveyed wildlife in Labrador, he turned his observations into quick-freezing methods that launched the modern frozen food industry — and a famous brand bears his name. Who was he?
Clarence Birdseye: American inventor, entrepreneur, and naturalist.

A summer migrant to Europe and Asia that winters in Africa, this bird tricks other species into raising its young by laying eggs that mimic the host's, and even disguises itself as a hawk — what bird is it?
Common cuckoo: Species of bird. It is a brood parasite, which means it lays eggs in the nests of other bird species, particularly of dunnocks, meadow pipits, and reed warblers.
Nicknamed the mosquito hawk, which long-legged insect of the superfamily Tipuloidea is often mistaken for an oversized mosquito?
Crane fly: Superfamily of flies. The larvae of crane flies are known commonly as leatherjackets.
This World Wide Web content sits on overlay networks that use the Internet but cannot be reached with an ordinary browser. What does reaching it require?
The dark web is World Wide Web content that exists on darknets — overlay networks that use the Internet but require specific software, configurations or authorization to access.
Produced by the enzyme 5α-reductase acting on a more familiar male sex hormone, this compound is a more potent driver of prostate growth, sebum, and body hair — which hormone?
Sometimes called 'word blindness,' this learning disability makes it hard to spell, sound out words, and read quickly, and often co-occurs with ADHD — what is it?
The tallest and heaviest of all living penguins, this flightless Antarctic bird can top 45 kilograms and sports bright-yellow ear patches — which species is it?
Emperor penguin: Large flightless seabird endemic to Antarctica.
This Marine-turned-professor's 1981 memoir about fighting at Peleliu and Okinawa later inspired Ken Burns's The War and HBO's The Pacific, where he was played by Joseph Mazzello — who is he?
Made up mostly of undigested food broken down by gut bacteria, this bodily waste is expelled through the anus and can even be dried for fuel or used as fertilizer — what is it?
Feces: Solid or semisolid remains of undigested food.

First described by 19th-century French psychiatrists Charles Lasègue and Jules Falret, this rare condition — also called shared psychotic disorder — lets one person's delusion spread to another. What is it called?

Folie à deux: Shared psychosis, a psychotic disorder. The disorder, first conceptualized in 19th century French psychiatry by Charles Lasègue and Jules Falret, is also known as Lasègue–Falret syndrome.

Named after Scottish naturalist Alexander Garden and first proposed in 1753 by botanist Jane Colden, this fragrant flowering genus in the coffee family is native to Africa, Asia and Australia — which plant genus?
Gardenia: Genus of flowering plants in the coffee family Rubiaceae.
Nicknamed the blue dragon, this pelagic sea slug floats upside down using surface tension and a stomach gas bubble, and feeds on the Portuguese man o' war — what is it?
With long, whip-like antennae and a global range except Antarctica, this insect family — known as true crickets — includes burrowing giants that dig meter-deep tunnels. What is the family called?
Gryllidae: Family of crickets. The family Gryllidae contains the subfamilies and genera which entomologists now term true crickets.
This German physicist was the first to conclusively demonstrate the electromagnetic waves predicted by James Clerk Maxwell's equations — who is he?
This genus of great apes emerged from Australopithecus and includes modern humans alongside extinct relatives, with chimpanzees and bonobos as its closest living kin — what genus is it?
Homo: Genus of hominins. Homo erectus and Homo neanderthalensis) classified as either ancestral or closely related to modern humans, collectively called archaic humans.

In this heart condition, the muscle walls, especially the wall between the ventricles, thicken without an obvious cause, weakening the heart's pumping and sometimes disrupting its electrical signals — which condition?

Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: Enlargement of the heart muscle. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM, or HOCM when obstructive) is a condition in which muscle tissues of the heart become thickened without an obvious cause.
Practitioners of this medical specialty are called internists in North America but simply 'physicians' in Britain, and often juggle patients with complex, multi-system disease — what field is it?
Internal medicine: Medical specialty dealing with adult diseases.
A PayPal engineer who built its real-time anti-fraud system, he co-founded a famous video site and uploaded its very first clip, 'Me at the zoo,' back in April 2005. Who is he?
Jawed Karim: American entrepreneur and software engineer (born 1979)
This evergreen conifer in the cypress family has the largest geographical range of any woody plant on Earth, spanning the cool temperate Northern Hemisphere. What is it?
Juniperus communis: Species of tree in the cypress family.
Derived from the design of the Vought F-8 Crusader, this subsonic carrier-based light attack aircraft replaced the Douglas Skyhawk and saw extensive action in the Vietnam War — which aircraft?
LTV A-7 Corsair II: American attack aircraft family.
This Chinese herbalist, martial artist, and tactical advisor died in 1933 having allegedly been born in 1677 — a longevity claim gerontologists dismiss as myth. Who was he?
Li Ching-Yuen: Chinese herbalist (died 1933). Li's year of birth was alleged to be 1677, though his true age has never been determined.
This Berkeley professor gave us "fuzzy" everything — fuzzy sets, fuzzy logic, fuzzy control — proposing a whole branch of mathematics for reasoning with imprecision. Who was he?
Known by the common English name 'mallow,' this plant genus bears palmately lobed leaves and five-petaled flowers ranging from pink to white — which genus?
Originally designated the DC-9 Series 80, this five-abreast single-aisle airliner first flew in October 1979 and entered service with launch customer Swissair the following year — what jet is it?
McDonnell Douglas MD-80: Jet airliner model, series based on the DC-9.
Despite little formal schooling, this self-taught English scientist uncovered the principles behind electromagnetic induction and established the concept of the electromagnetic field — who is he?
Michael Faraday: English chemist and physicist (1791–1867)
Born in Taiwan but naturalized in Japan, this businessman invented the world's first prepackaged instant noodle brand and later created Cup Noodles — who is he?
Momofuku Ando: Taiwanese-Japanese inventor and businessman (1910–2007)
Also called flystrike, this parasitic condition occurs when fly larvae infest and feed on the tissue of a living animal — what is it?
This 17th-century Dane was a pioneer of both anatomy and geology — he doubted that fossils "grew" in the ground — before becoming a Catholic bishop and being beatified by the Church. Who was he?
Nicolas Steno: Danish scientist and Catholic bishop (1638 – 1686)
This order of predatory flying insects includes dragonflies and damselflies, whose aquatic larvae are voracious carnivores capable of overpowering small fish and tadpoles — what is it called?
Odonata: Order of insects that includes the dragonflies and damselflies. The adults are superb aerial hunters and their legs are specialised for catching prey in flight.

Powered by NADH and FADH₂ handed off from glycolysis and the citric acid cycle, this mitochondrial pathway is how nearly all aerobic organisms produce ATP — far more efficiently than fermentation. What's it called?
Oxidative phosphorylation: Metabolic pathway. Oxidative phosphorylation uses these molecules and O2 to produce ATP, which is used throughout the cell whenever energy is needed.
First domesticated in Neolithic China, this tree's fruit comes in a fuzzy form and a glossy-skinned twin called the nectarine — what fruit, a rose-family relative of the cherry and plum?
Peach: Type of fruit tree, or its fruit.
The body produces about a quart of this substance daily to trap airborne particles and bacteria — coughed up, it's also known as sputum. What is it?
Phlegm: Mucus produced by the respiratory system (excluding the nasal passages)
Commonly called frangipani, this fragrant flowering shrub native to Mexico and the Caribbean is now a beloved ornamental in Hawaii and desert climates of Arabia — what genus is it?
Plumeria: Genus of flowering plants endemic to the Americas.
Defined as supervising a team to hit all its goals within three primary constraints — scope, time, and budget — what is this discipline?
Project management: Practice of leading the work of a team to achieve goals and criteria at a specified time.

Found across Africa, Asia, and Australia, this family of nonvenomous snakes — including some of the world's largest — must coil around prey and squeeze it into cardiac arrest before swallowing it whole. What is the family?
Pythonidae: Family of snakes. The taxonomy of pythons has evolved, and they are now known to be more closely related to sunbeam snakes and the Mexican burrowing python.

Nicknamed 'the Thud' by its crews, this Mach 2 jet flew most of the early Vietnam War's strike missions and became the only American aircraft ever pulled from combat over unsustainable losses — which plane?
Republic F-105 Thunderchief: US Air Force supersonic fighter-bomber.
Native to tropical Africa and the Indian subcontinent, this medium-sized parrot has established wild populations worldwide after pet-trade escapees adapted brilliantly to city life — which bird?

Rose-ringed parakeet: Species of bird. The rose-ringed parakeet (Psittacula krameri), also known as the ring-necked parakeet, is a medium-sized parrot in the genus Psittacula, of the family Psittaculidae.
This Sapporo-born programmer rose to become Nintendo's fourth president, betting on novel, entertaining games over the most powerful hardware — who is he?
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
Satoru Iwata: Japanese video game executive (1959–2015)
Domesticated more than 3,000 years ago and prized for having one of the highest oil contents of any seed, which crop is also known as benne?
Sesame: Plant cultivated for its edible seeds.

Once extracted from the ashes of certain salt-absorbing plants and now produced from ordinary salt and limestone via the Solvay process, this alkaline compound is also known as washing soda or soda ash — what is it?
Sodium carbonate: Chemical compound. Sodium carbonate (also known as washing soda, soda ash, sal soda, and soda crystals) is the inorganic compound with the formula Na2CO3 and its various hydrates.
A luminous ball of plasma held together by its own gravity, the closest example to Earth is the Sun — what celestial object is this?
Star: Large self-illuminated object in space.
Striking suddenly and resolving — one way or another — within 8 to 10 hours, this mysterious epidemic first hit England in 1485 and vanished after a final outbreak in 1551 — what was it called?
Sweating sickness: Contagious disease in Europe, 1485–1551.
Element 117 carries the second-highest atomic number of any known element and is named for a U.S. state where key research institutions sit — which element is it?
Tennessine: Chemical element with atomic number 117 (Ts)
Known as linden, lime, or basswood depending on the region, this genus of about 30 tree species is the only one in its plant family to form ectomycorrhizal fungal partnerships. What genus is it?
Tilia: Plant genus. Tilia is a genus of about 30 species of trees or bushes, native throughout most of the temperate Northern Hemisphere.
Feeding exclusively on vertebrate blood across tropical Africa, this biting fly folds its wings completely over its abdomen at rest and spreads trypanosomiasis — which insect?
Tsetse fly: Genus of disease-spreading insects.

Discovered in 1801 by a Spanish-Mexican scientist but only confirmed as a new element in 1830, this hard silvery-grey transition metal takes its name from a Scandinavian goddess of beauty — what element is it?
Vanadium: Chemical element with atomic number 23 (V)
Equal to seven days, this standard calendrical period sits between a single day and a month — despite ancient Egyptians preferring a ten-day version, what unit of time is it?
Week: Time unit equal to seven days. The days of the week are often used to set work days, rest days, and holy days.

Named after a 19th-century British scientist but actually first developed by Leonhard Euler in 1727, this mechanical property measures a solid material's stiffness under tension or compression — what is it called?

Young's modulus: Mechanical property that measures stiffness of a solid material. As such, Young's modulus is similar and proportional to the spring constant in Hooke's law, but with dimensions of pressure instead of force per distance.

Thulium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for thulium is Tm. Thulium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tm and atomic number 69.
